title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §10° of a late, numbered part of the 'Longue Marche' continuation (manuscript pages ~791–792). Its title is 'Les sous-multiplicités M_{ρ,σ}[0], M_{ρ,σ}(0), M_{ρ,σ}(1/2), M^♮_{ρ,σ}(−j), …'. 'Multiplicité' is Grothendieck's word for a stack or orbifold-type object; here the objects behave like group objects, written with underlines.

The ambient object is M_{ρ,σ}. Labels ρ and σ are presumably the two special elliptic points or torsion generators of orders 6 and 4 (or 3 and 2) of the modular situation; the order-12 group D_12^* fits this. It is presented as an iterated fibre product N_ρ^? ×_γ N_σ^♮ ×_γ G_{ρ,σ}, viewed inside the full product. Concretely it is the set of triples (a,b,u) whose images under the structure maps γ_ρ, γ_σ, γ_G into a common target agree.

Three sub-objects are cut out by conditions on the third coordinate u:
- (196) M[0] = {(a,b,u) : u ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}}, where Z_{ρ,σ} is a distinguished subgroup (probably the centre or centraliser) of G_{ρ,σ}. Hence M[0] ≅ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ Z_{ρ,σ}, which maps isomorphically onto a group S_0Γ_{ρ,σ}. A side remark says that the closure of M[0] lies in the closure of M^♮.
- (197) Z(0) ⊂ Z is the fixed subgroup of the D_12^* action. That action is the one realising G_{ρ,σ} as a semidirect product ('produit ½ direct') in (150), (151). One sets M(0) = N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ Z(0).
- (198) gives a diagram: M(0) ⊂ M[0], each mapping with degree 2 onto SΓ(0) ↪ S_0Γ, and SΓ(0) maps 2:1 onto Γ_{ρ,σ}(0). These are index-2 or central-extension bookkeeping steps, in the way SL_2 relates to PSL_2.
- (199) In the semidirect-product coordinates of the previous page, M(0) = μ·(λ,0), with λ ∈ ΓG_a and 0 ∈ ΓS^+. That is, modulo μ_ρ it is D_12^*·G_a, embedded via the obvious inclusion G_a → G_a × S^+, as the next page confirms in (200).

The purpose is to make explicit a filtration or family of distinguished subgroups of the 'modular' group object M_{ρ,σ}, compatible with its semidirect decomposition D_12^* ⋉ (G_a × S^+). This presumably serves to compare with the discrete groups Γ_{ρ,σ}, SΓ_{ρ,σ}. The next page adds M(1/2) = {u = b}, a section isomorphic to Γ_{ρ,σ}.
errors: No mathematical error is detectable. The constructions are definitional.

Equation numbering is reused: (195)–(196) on this page clash with (195)–(196) on the previous page. The next page refers to 'la description (195)' in the sense of the previous page's semidirect-product isomorphisms. This is a minor bookkeeping inconsistency.
The degree-2 claims in (198) are asserted without proof. They depend on Z/Z(0) and on μ_ρ data not visible on this page.

ideas.what: Presentation of a group object as an iterated fibre product over a common quotient and cutting out subgroups by conditions on one factor
ideas.modern_name: fibre product of groups / subgroup defined by centraliser and fixed-point conditions

ideas.what: Fixed subgroup Z(0) of the D_12^* action in a semidirect product, and the resulting subgroup D_12^*·G_a
ideas.modern_name: fixed points of a finite group action / semidirect product decomposition

ideas.what: Index-2 tower M(0) → SΓ(0) → Γ(0) relating 'S' (special/spin) and plain versions of modular-type groups attached to elliptic points ρ, σ
ideas.modern_name: SL_2 vs PSL_2-type central extensions; stabilisers of elliptic points in the modular group
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the discussion of M_{1,1} and its fundamental groupoid in the Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche, but unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is internal bookkeeping: definitions of sub-objects of an already-constructed semidirect-product group object, with routine index-2 diagrams. Without the earlier pages the objects cannot be pinned down precisely, but nothing here appears to be a new result or a new connection.
transcription_corrections: '½ dirait' should be read as '½ direct', i.e. 'produit ½ direct' = semidirect product. Examples: 'comme produit ½ direct', and 'le facteur ½ direct D_12^*'.
'N_σ^{≤}' is more likely N_σ^♮ (natural sign), consistent with M^♮ on adjacent pages; likewise 'M'_{ρ,σ}(−j)' is probably M^♮_{ρ,σ}(−j).
The bottom annotation under (λ,0) reads 'ΓG_a  Γ𝔊^+' (or ΓS^+), not 'ΓG_m', as confirmed by (200) on the next page.
'On utilise la présentation[?]' is probably 'On utilise la présentation' (or 'le plongement').
In (196), the deleted target after the isomorphism is replaced by S_0Γ_{ρ,σ}.
The marginal note reads roughly: 'NB Z_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} le fixat. du facteur ½ direct D_12^* de G_{ρ,σ} dans (150); il pourrait[?] … G_{ρ,σ}(0)'.
